source: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition (1 May 2026)

questions.stemEn: A child presents with a skin rash described as gloves-and-socks syndrome. What is the most likely causative organism?
questions.explanationAr: وجود papular-purpuric gloves-and-socks syndrome يوجّه في المصدر إلى Parvovirus B19. الطفح يكون غالبًا مؤلمًا أو حاكًا ومحدودًا نسبيًا لليدين والقدمين بعد viral prodrome.
questions.reasoningEn: The source identifies parvovirus B19 as the most frequent cause of papular-purpuric gloves-and-socks syndrome.

incorrectOptionsAr.A: Coxsackievirus A16 يرتبط أكثر بـ hand-foot-and-mouth disease، وليس النمط المذكور في السؤال.
incorrectOptionsAr.C: Group A Streptococcus قد يسبب scarlet fever أو soft-tissue infection، لكنه ليس السبب النموذجي لهذا syndrome.

questions.clinicalPearl: Gloves-and-socks purpura is a classic board clue for Parvovirus B19.

image.description: Original rash image referenced in the source question.

questions.stemEn: A 6-month-old boy presents with low-grade fever and bilateral cheek lesions described as cold panniculitis. His mother reports tooth eruption and use of a cold teething ring. What is your recommendation?
questions.explanationAr: ارتباط آفات الخدين بالتعرّض المباشر للبرد من teething ring يتوافق مع cold panniculitis أو popsicle panniculitis. المصدر يذكر أنها غالبًا self-limited وتتحسن تلقائيًا خلال أسابيع، لذلك الاختيار هو reassurance.
questions.reasoningEn: Cold panniculitis in infants follows local cold exposure and usually resolves spontaneously.

incorrectOptionsAr.B: السياق يربط الآفات بالبرد مباشرة، ولا يدعم إجراء Parvovirus serology كخطوة أولى.

questions.clinicalPearl: Cold objects used for teething can trigger self-limited cheek panniculitis in infants.
managementSteps: Reassure caregivers and avoid further local cold exposure.

image.description: Original bilateral cheek lesion image referenced in source.

questions.stemEn: A child presents with non-purulent conjunctivitis, exudative pharyngitis and a viral prodrome. Anterior cervical lymph nodes are enlarged and rapid strep testing is negative. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanationAr: اجتماع non-purulent conjunctivitis مع exudative pharyngitis وviral prodrome مع RST سلبي هو clue قوي لـ Adenovirus، وبالذات pharyngoconjunctival fever.
questions.reasoningEn: Adenovirus can cause exudative pharyngitis together with non-purulent conjunctivitis and cervical lymphadenopathy.

incorrectOptionsAr.B: EBV يميل إلى posterior cervical lymphadenopathy مع fatigue وقد يصاحبه hepatosplenomegaly.
incorrectOptionsAr.C: Coxsackievirus يرتبط أكثر بـ herpangina أو hand-foot-and-mouth disease.

questions.clinicalPearl: Conjunctivitis plus pharyngitis is a classic adenovirus combination.

verification.referenceNotes: Source explanation cites PREP 2018 and MedStudy.

questions.stemEn: A 4-year-old child has fever, cough, runny nose, non-purulent conjunctivitis and abdominal pain. Antibiotics did not improve the illness. Examination shows exudative pharyngitis without lymph-node enlargement. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanationAr: وجود conjunctivitis غير قيحي مع URTI symptoms وexudative pharyngitis وعدم الاستجابة للمضاد الحيوي يدعم Adenovirus أكثر من bacterial pharyngitis.
questions.reasoningEn: The source treats this as another adenoviral pharyngoconjunctival illness.

incorrectOptionsAr.B: الصورة لا تذكر السمات الكلاسيكية لـ EBV مثل posterior nodes أو hepatosplenomegaly.
incorrectOptionsAr.C: لا توجد vesicular posterior oral lesions أو HFMD pattern.
incorrectOptionsAr.D: وجود conjunctivitis وcoryza يجعل GAS أقل احتمالًا.

questions.clinicalPearl: Coryza/conjunctivitis argue against classic GAS pharyngitis.

verification.referenceNotes: Source points to the preceding adenovirus explanation.

questions.stemEn: A patient presents with symptoms and signs suggestive of infectious mononucleosis and an accompanying image. Which diagnostic test would you request?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يذكر أن suspected infectious mononucleosis يمكن تقييمه بـ heterophile antibody test مثل Monospot أو EBV-specific antibody testing؛ لذلك من الخيارات المتاحة اختير Monospot.
questions.reasoningEn: The source recommends a heterophile test or EBV-specific antibody testing for suspected infectious mononucleosis.

incorrectOptionsAr.A: CMV IgM لا يثبت EBV infectious mononucleosis.
incorrectOptionsAr.B: Throat culture قد يفيد لتقييم streptococcal coinfection لكنه ليس الاختبار المقصود لتأكيد EBV هنا.
incorrectOptionsAr.D: ASO يدل على استجابة سابقة لـ streptococcal infection ولا يشخّص EBV.

questions.clinicalPearl: In suspected EBV mononucleosis, heterophile testing or EBV-specific serology is used depending on age and context.
diagnosticSteps: Heterophile antibody testing or EBV-specific antibody testing as supported by the source.

questions.stemEn: A patient with infectious mononucleosis has exudative pharyngitis. There was no skin rash initially, but a rash developed later. Monospot is positive and ASO is negative. No antibiotic exposure is stated. What is the most likely cause of the rash?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر نفسه يضع علامة استفهام على Amoxicillin لأن السؤال لا يذكر أخذ antibiotic. كما يوضح أن rash في infectious mononucleosis قد يظهر مع antibiotics أو حتى بدونها. لذلك لا نعتمد B كإجابة نهائية قبل المراجعة.
questions.reasoningEn: The recalled key is uncertain and the stem omits antibiotic exposure, so the source does not support a definitive verified answer.
questions.clinicalPearl: Do not infer amoxicillin exposure when the recall stem does not state it.

verification.referenceNotes: Source explicitly labels the recalled answer B with uncertainty.

questions.stemEn: An infant develops a skin rash just after the fever resolves. Which virus is the probable cause?
questions.explanationAr: الـhigh-yield clue هو fever resolves then rash appears؛ هذا هو pattern الكلاسيكي لـ roseola infantum، والمصدر يختار HHV-6.
questions.reasoningEn: Rash emerging as the fever resolves is the classic roseola pattern in the source.
questions.clinicalPearl: Roseola: high fever first, rash after defervescence.

questions.stemEn: An infant presents with a typical picture of roseola infantum. Which complication or association is known with this infection?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يذكر أن roseola المرتبطة غالبًا بـ HHV-6B قد تترافق مع febrile seizures، ولذلك هذا association مهم للاختبار.
questions.reasoningEn: The source notes febrile seizures as a recognized complication of primary HHV-6B infection.
questions.clinicalPearl: Roseola is a classic viral trigger for febrile seizures.

questions.stemEn: A child has a rash that starts on the face and spreads cephalocaudally, palpable cervical lymph nodes, and Forchheimer spots. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanationAr: الـclues في المصدر هي rash يبدأ من الوجه وينتشر للأسفل، lymphadenopathy، وForchheimer spots؛ وهذا pattern يوجّه إلى Rubella.
questions.reasoningEn: The source associates cephalocaudal rash, lymphadenopathy and Forchheimer spots with rubella.

incorrectOptionsAr.B: EBV لا يعطي هذا exanthem pattern مع Forchheimer spots كعلامة مميزة.

questions.clinicalPearl: Forchheimer spots plus a mild cephalocaudal exanthem is a rubella clue.
